external_entities.name: library member
external_entities.description: A person who borrows, renews or reserves books through the library app, and uses self-service kiosks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.

external_entities.name: desk staff
external_entities.description: Library staff who use the circulation page to extend loans, clear account blocks and mark books returned.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
external_entities.notes: Everyone at the desk uses the same shared login; the individual staff member and branch cannot be identified from the history.

processes.name: library app
processes.description: An application on members' phones that calls the lending API for borrowing, renewal and reservation actions.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

processes.name: lending API
processes.description: The REST API through which loans are accessed and changed. It checks loan rules and reads and writes the loans database.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: Exposure disagreement: Lending service note says "The lending API is internal-only." Interview transcript says "The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet." Authentication is uncertain: Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look."

processes.name: self-service kiosk
processes.description: A branch kiosk where a member scans a library card and books being borrowed or returned, then sends loan and return records to the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.

data_stores.name: loans database
data_stores.description: The single database containing members, loans and reservations, including member names, email addresses, home addresses and full borrowing history.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: The interview corrects the earlier description of two databases: "We merged those in the spring. It's one loans database now. The old reservations database is gone."

data_flows.name: renew or reserve loans
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member, and the API checks the loan rules and writes the change.
data_flows.data_description: Book and member details; renewal or reservation request

data_flows.name: send loans and returns
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.data_description: Loan and return records, including scanned member card and book details

data_flows.name: change loan records
data_flows.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
data_flows.notes: Staff use a circulation page served by the lending API and a shared login.

data_flows.name: read and write loan data
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.

trust_boundaries.name: branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network used by branch kiosks and desk staff.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data centre where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The network over which phones talk directly to the lending API.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet.

assumptions.assumption: The loans database is confidential because it contains names, email addresses, home addresses and full borrowing histories.
assumptions.basis: Interview transcript states: "Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database."

assumptions.assumption: The branch network is a network trust boundary because it is a distinct network location for kiosks and desk staff within the library environment.
assumptions.basis: The source places kiosks and desk staff on the branch network.

assumptions.assumption: The council data centre is a network trust boundary because it is a distinct network location where the API and database run.
assumptions.basis: The source places the lending API and loans database in the council data centre.

assumptions.assumption: The internet is a network trust boundary because it is the distinct network through which phones reach the lending API.
assumptions.basis: The interview states that phones talk directly to the lending API over the internet.
